changelog: Replace C4 to address the primary finding: require verbal complexes (negation, resultatives, verb–object compounds, auxiliaries/aspect markers, tightly bound predicates) to stay with their complements and advise how a GOOD cut looks (after a completed predicate and with punctuation/quotes attached).

Replace C3 to keep left-headed modifier guidance but add the measured tradeoff: do not preserve multi-token names when that would isolate punctuation, reporting verbs, or core predicates—split names if needed so predicates and their punctuation remain intact.

Replace C4 to require verbal complexes (negation, resultatives, VO compounds, auxiliaries/aspect markers, tightly bound predicate material) stay with their verb/complements and to state what a good cut looks like (after a completed predicate, with punctuation/closing particles attached).

Replace C8 to deprioritize preserving multi-token names when doing so would isolate punctuation, reporting verbs, or core predicates; prefer splits that keep predicates and their punctuation/quotes intact.
Replace E1 with labeled example cmn_hans_cn_236 to teach the model about splits that orphan negated or tightly bound predicate material (primary finding evidence).
Replace E2 with labeled example cmn_hans_cn_398 to show cases where verb complexes are split and produce high contradiction scores.
Replace E3 with labeled example cmn_hans_cn_979 to illustrate resultative/verb-object bindings that must stay intact for entailment.
Replace E4 with labeled example cmn_hans_cn_880 to include another measured instance from the primary finding set (tight predicate/complement splits).
Delete E3 and E4 to reduce prompt length substantially (remove long example units that inflate size).

Insert new core-principle after C8: require verbal complexes to stay with their complements and prioritize keeping predicates/punctuation intact over preserving multi-token names, with guidance on what a good cut looks like.
